text: 📸 Mañanera del Pueblo — Toluca, Estado de México, 22 de julio de 2026

🇲🇽💧 Flood protection for 10 million people in the Valley of Mexico’s east. The Churubusco-Xochiaca pumping station and the Pinos collector are complete — cutting flood risk for more than 10 million residents of the eastern Valley of Mexico. — CONAGUA report, Mañanera del Pueblo from Toluca A structural answer to the flooding that hit working-class colonias every rainy season for decades. Part of the State of Mexico’s hydraulic infrastructure investment.

🇲🇽🚆 5.3 billion pesos for Mexico’s poorest east — not for luxury towers. The Plan Integral del Oriente: over 5.3 billion pesos, 202 water works between 2025 and 2026, six new high schools, 208 "Safe Pathways" routes, and the start of an elevated trolleybus viaduct toward Ixtapaluca. — Infrastructure report, Mañanera del Pueblo from Toluca Public investment aimed at the historically marginalized eastern edge of the megalopolis — schools, water, transit, and lit-and-patrolled streets for working-class neighborhoods.

🇲🇽✊ "Power hasn’t gone to her head. She’s the same teacher she always was." "Delfina has many virtues, and something very special: power hasn’t gone to her head. She’s an honest woman, a hard worker — the same teacher from when she taught in her classroom. A humble woman." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on Governor Delfina Gómez Delfina Gómez — a former rural teacher and the first woman to govern the State of Mexico — hosted the conference in Toluca, where her administration reported gains in security, water, and infrastructure.

🇲🇽🔍 "There is no impunity." Sheinbaum on the Dafne case. "It is the state government that must carry out all the investigations and review how these centers are operating." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on the Dafne case in Tamaulipas Asked about the Dafne case at a state training academy in Tamaulipas, Sheinbaum clarified the probe falls to the state — not the Defense Ministry — since these are state-run centers. She reaffirmed that whoever must be investigated will be.

🇲🇽🎨 "To everyone applying to a school with an entrance exam: don’t cheat." "To all those who aspire to an educational institution with an admission exam — don’t commit any kind of fraud." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on the UNAM online exam After irregularities in UNAM’s first fully virtual admission exam, Sheinbaum said the fault wasn’t the university’s but a failure to account for AI in online testing — and urged education authorities to rethink how knowledge is measured.

🇲🇽🔍 Homicides down 58% in the State of Mexico — from 6.6 a day to 2.8. Between September 2024 and June 2026, average daily homicides in Mexico’s most populous state fell 58%. High-impact crime dropped 40%. — Security report, Mañanera del Pueblo from Toluca The result of an intelligence-led strategy and the Mando Unificado Oriente deployed across 15 municipalities since June 2025 — attention to root causes, not the old "war." The 4T model, measured in numbers.

🇲🇽🌎 "We’re going to wait." Sheinbaum stays calm as Washington readies tariffs on 60 countries. "We’re going to wait. Last week the Economy Ministry presented every argument for why there shouldn’t be higher tariffs on Mexico — but we’re going to wait." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on the coming US tariff round The US is weighing new tariffs on ~60 countries. Mexico already delivered its technical and commercial case. Sheinbaum receives US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer at the National Palace on Thursday.

🇲🇽🏠 MEXICO'S MORTGAGE BOOK HITS A RECORD 1.5 TRILLION PESOS

Even with high interest rates, Mexico's housing-credit portfolio reached a record 1.513 trillion pesos at the end of May — up 4.9% in nominal terms from 1.442 trillion a year earlier, on Banco de México data reported by El Economista. Commercial banks now project 3–5% mortgage growth through 2026, with the market reactivating since March.

🇲🇽🛢️ 83% OF MEXICO'S GAS STATIONS NOW HOLD THE LINE ON DIESEL

8,481 gas stations — 83% of the sector — have joined the government's voluntary accord to keep diesel under 27 pesos a liter (25.39 in the border zone). Pemex backs it by feeding stations through its own last-mile distribution to cut transport costs. While global crude climbs, Mexico chose to shield the consumer, not the refiner's margin — and the 1,721 holdouts still overcharging are now the visible outliers.
